channel.title: World
channel.description: The Washington Post World section provides information and analysis of breaking world news stories. In addition to our world news and video, Post World News offers discussions and blogs on major international news and economic issues.

item.title: Beijing expands purge of top generals
item.dc:creator: Joshua Yang
item.description: President Xi Jinping is targeting officers affiliated with previously ousted leaders, analysts say, even as Beijing seeks to project power across the Indo-Pacific.

item.title: Sliman Mansour has died. His art became a symbol of Palestinian resilience.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Smith
item.description: For more than 50 years, he explored Palestinian life and history in his paintings. His work became increasingly political after he spent time in jail.

item.title: Ka-nyet! Kanye West concerts canceled in Russia.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ilyushina
item.description: Two sold-out shows in St. Petersburg were scrapped, highlighting wartime ambivalence about Western culture and the rapper’s past antisemitic remarks.

item.title: Trump says he has secured a vast U.S. stake in Venezuelan oil industry
item.dc:creator: Evan Halper, Karen DeYoung, Anthony Faiola, Samantha Schmidt
item.description: The plan involves the United States taking more direct control over Venezuelan reserves as crime and steep logistical challenges discourage private investors.

item.title: At least 540 killed in floods; search on for hundreds missing at Nepal-China border
item.dc:creator: Aoife Walsh, Joshua Yang, N. Kirkpatrick
item.description: Fears of further flooding complicated recovery efforts, as authorities searched for people missing after floods struck the Himalayan border between Nepal and China.

item.title: Trump’s grab for Greenland rattles Iceland, which considers joining E.U.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Francis, Beatriz Ríos
item.description: Iceland will decide whether to restart talks on joining the European Union in a referendum on Saturday, with President Donald Trump's threat to annex Greenland a motivating factor.

item.title: Volkswagen CEO warns German workers of sweeping layoffs to come
item.dc:creator: Maegan Vazquez
item.description: The automaker, one of the nation’s biggest employers, could shed tens of thousands of jobs amid global market shifts driven by electrification, AI and autonomous driving.

item.title: Uganda declared Ebola-free even as Congo faces deadly, fast-growing epidemic
item.dc:creator: Rael Ombuor
item.description: Uganda's final Ebola patient was discharged from hospital care on July 16.

item.title: Rescuers race to find survivors after Himalayan floods kill more than 350
item.dc:creator: Aoife Walsh, Joshua Yang
item.description: Hundreds of people, including more than 600 tourists, remain missing after the floods hit the Nepal-China border.
